key_insight: Neuronally-enriched extracellular vesicle synaptopodin is a blood-based marker of synaptic integrity that predicts disability progression in progressive multiple sclerosis, especially secondary progressive MS.
clinical_relevance: If validated further, this biomarker could help identify people with progressive MS at higher risk of worsening and improve monitoring beyond standard neurofilament light chain (NfL).
method: Measured synaptopodin in neuronal-enriched extracellular vesicles (NEVs) from blood.
Analyzed two independent cohorts: SPRINT-MS (n=184) and a real-world validation cohort (n=268).
Linked baseline and longitudinal biomarker levels to disability progression and MRI measures of brain atrophy/microstructural integrity.
evidence_signal: Across two cohorts, higher baseline NEV synaptopodin was associated with lower risk of confirmed disability progression and showed stronger predictive performance than NfL in SPMS, with replication in the validation cohort.
watch_item: This is promising but still observational/biomarker-based, so broader external validation and standardized assay workflows are needed before routine clinical use.
paper_title: A Blood-Based Synaptic Biomarker in Neuronally-Enriched Extracellular Vesicles Predicts Disability Progression in Progressive Multiple Sclerosis
